Inherited four missing original v15 BarCache.PixelProbe.dll artifacts; never replaced by rebuilds

ReduceMotion is application supplied; host applications must bridge operating-system/user motion preferences into this property
AM02 independent per-series delay/progress remain open
Animation stationary-pointer readouts do not continuously follow moving data; functional frame timing is not a C4 performance result

Export capture/render/copy still executes synchronously on the UI thread, and the codec call cannot be interrupted within compression; formal UI capture/encoding throughput, peak memory, concurrent-chart and soak budgets remain C4 work.
Future chart-family/polar/3D/stacked/LOD annotation contracts, interactive editing and advanced annotation label placement remain open.
Future chart families, High/Low/Weight and additional geometry animation; exit fades, per-point staggering and arbitrary style/axis-topology transitions remain unimplemented.
Formal animation frame-budget, tail latency, CPU/memory and soak performance have not been measured in this functional batch.
StorageProvider save-picker real interaction and cancellation still require physical Windows/Linux desktop verification; programmatic stream/file evidence does not certify picker interaction.

File cancellation is observed at the last token check before commit; a request racing between that check and File.Move, or arriving after commit, cannot roll back the published file. Temporary cleanup is best effort under IO/access failures; controlled validation directories were independently checked for residue.

Export Background composites the requested canvas without automatically changing chart foreground styles; applications must choose matching foreground/background colors. Pale dark-theme text on a white/light export canvas can have low contrast.

JPEG is lossy: chroma subsampling can change thin colored strokes even at default quality90; original-color pixel equality is not a JPEG guarantee. There is currently no independent chroma-subsampling option. Geometry/chroma is validated separately; further fidelity controls and formal encoding/memory budgets remain C4 work.

packageExportScope: Headless package consumers validate successful encoding or explicit backend failure with no published file; actual native JPEG/PNG bytes, pixels and metadata are separately proved by Windows/WSLg exports. Caller-owned stream write failures may leave partial output.

pngEncoderQuantizationContract.synchronous: Existing platform PNG encoder retained for compatibility
pngEncoderQuantizationContract.asynchronous: Unpremultiplied RGBA capture plus managed stb PNG writer

asynchronousExportScope: UI dispatcher captures an immutable RGBA snapshot; a worker encodes and writes it. One export lease per chart; explicit cancellation throws without ExportFailed. Codec compression is one bounded indivisible stage, with cancellation before/after that stage and between chunked writes. Caller streams remain open and may contain partial output; local files commit via a same-directory temporary-file replacement. Commit is not rolled back by cancellation arriving after the move.
nativeAnimationScope: Current candidate also revalidates the C207 real-clock native-frame, numeric projection, pause/delay and 96/144/192 DPI current-frame PNG contracts. This is functional validation, not formal animation frame-budget/CPU/memory qualification.
